test_title: SSC MTS (2022) Official Paper (Held On: 10 May, 2023 Shift 2)
subject: general
question:
Three statements are given followed by two conclusions numbered I and II. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements.

**Statements:**

Some towns are cities.

Some cities are villages.

All villages are states.

**Conclusions:**

I. Some towns are not villages.

II. Some states are cities.

options.text: Both conclusions I and II follow
Neither conclusion I nor II follows

solution:
Given Statements:

Some towns are cities.

Some cities are villages.

All villages are states.

The least possible Venn diagram for the given statement is:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9c862bfbf460abaa7e6282241181a5e7534a6f55a1006a8a4e46631c40a77c28.png] 

Conclusions:

I. Some towns are not villages - False (Because, No definite relation given between towns and villages, so it can be possible only).

II. Some states are cities - **True **(Because, Some cities are villages and All villages are states, so those part of cities which is villages will also states).

So, Only conclusion II follows.

Hence, the correct answer is "Option 1".
